title: Two Coworkers Discuss Umm Salamah's Long Journey
script: Dewi: [thoughtful] Fajar, I've been reading about Umm Salamah lately, and her story keeps surprising me every time I return to it.
Fajar: [curious] I don't know much about her. What makes her story so unusual compared to the others?
Dewi: [reflective] Well, when she and her husband decided to migrate to Madinah, her own family stopped them at the city gate.
Fajar: [surprised] Wait, her family physically prevented her from leaving? That seems shocking, since migration was supposed to be voluntary.
Dewi: [sadly] Exactly. They took her son away from her arms and forced her husband to travel without them, alone and worried.
Fajar: [wincing] So she was separated from her husband and her child at the same time? That sounds incredibly painful.
Dewi: [nodding] It was. She sat by that gate every single day for almost a year, crying quietly and waiting for news.
Fajar: [thoughtful] A year is a long time to wait, especially not knowing whether you would ever see your family again.
Dewi: [warmly] Eventually, her relatives felt ashamed of their cruelty, so they finally allowed her to travel and reunite with her son.
Fajar: [relieved] That must have felt like the happiest day of her entire life, after so much suffering and uncertainty.
Dewi: [smiling] It truly was. And later, after her husband passed away, she became one of the Prophet's wives, known for her sharp wisdom.
Fajar: [interested] Wisdom? Can you give me an example of that?
Dewi: [explaining] During a difficult treaty, when the men hesitated to follow an instruction, she quietly suggested a solution that solved everything calmly.
Fajar: [amazed] So her advice actually changed the outcome of an important political moment? That's impressive for anyone.
Dewi: [reflective] Exactly. Whenever I feel forgotten or unheard, I remember Umm Salamah waiting patiently by that gate for a whole year.
Fajar: [smiling] That's a powerful reminder. Patience really can lead somewhere, even after the longest and hardest waiting.
